advertisements.title: Blessing & Turnover of the New Firetruck 🚒
advertisements.description:
Blessing & Turnover of the New Firetruck 🚒

A meaningful day for the Municipality of Titay as we officially welcome and turn over our new Firetruck—a much-needed addition to strengthen our emergency response and fire protection capabilities.

Our heartfelt gratitude to Mayor Riorita “DONRIO” Martinez Castillo, RPh, for making the acquisition of this firetruck a priority and for her unwavering commitment to the safety and welfare of every Titayanon.

We likewise extend our sincere appreciation to the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), particularly SFO4 Neil Siaron, together with FSSUPT Nazrudyn M. Cablayan, DSC, FSSUPT Jacqueline S. Ortega, DSC, FSUPT Wilfredo A. David, DSC, and FSUPT Reggy A. Olmedo, DSC, for your invaluable support and dedication to strengthening fire protection and emergency response in our municipality.

Above all, our deepest gratitude to DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla for his support and for helping make this much-needed firetruck a reality for the people of Titay.

This firetruck is more than just equipment—it is an investment in safety, preparedness, and the protection of our people.

Daghang salamat sa tanan nga mitabang aron matuman kini nga panalangin para sa atong lungsod. Padayon ta sa pagserbisyo ug pagpanalipod sa matag Titayanon! ❤️🚒

#DASIGTITAY

advertisements.title: Matilum Cave Complex is a remarkable cave system that connects three barangays…
advertisements.description:
Matilum Cave Complex is a remarkable cave system that connects three barangays in the Municipality of Titay and Ipil; Mate, Timalang, and Lumbia. Locally, this natural wonder is more commonly known as Balangasan Cave. 

This hidden gem of Titay, showcases the municipality’s rich natural heritage and breathtaking beauty, waiting to be explored and protected for generations to come. 

Love Titay. Dasig Titay.❤️

P.S. This is still not open to the public yet. To those who wish to visit please coordinate with the Local Tourism in Titay and the DENR Office.

newsArticles.summary:
𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐄 
𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift B duty personnel provided immediate medical assistance to a walk-in male patient who arrived at the station complaining of injuries sustained in a vehicular accident. Upon arrival, the patient underwent a physical assessment, which revealed abrasions on his left knee and right elbow.
First aid was provided by thoroughly irrigating the wounds with normal saline solution, followed by the application of povidone-iodine (Betadine) and sterile gauze dressings to help prevent infection.
The patient refused transport to the nearest hospital for further medical evaluation. Duty personnel advised him of the importance of seeking immediate medical attention should his condition worsen. A Refusal of Transport Form (RTF) was thoroughly explained to the patient, which he acknowledged and signed.

𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: 0965-509-0944.
#SaBFPLigtasAngMayAlam
#TitayMFS
#EmergencyMedicalResponse
#WeServeToSave

newsArticles.summary:
𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐄 
𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay MFS Shift B duty personnel received a report of a medical emergency at Purok Doña Aurora, Achasol, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. The responding personnel were immediately dispatched and proceeded to the scene to provide the necessary medical care.
Upon arrival at the scene, the responding team found a 15-year-old female patient, approximately 39 weeks pregnant, standing at the roadside. The patient was conscious, alert, and oriented. Initial assessment revealed labor contractions occurring approximately every 20 minutes, with each contraction lasting about 2 minutes, accompanied by vaginal discharge.
First aid was provided by assisting the patient into a position of comfort while continuously monitoring her condition and preparing her for safe transport.
The patient was immediately transported to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center for further medical evaluation and management.
Upon arrival at Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center, Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, the patient was properly endorsed to the attending medical staff on duty.

𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: 0965-509-0944.

newsArticles.title: EARTHQUAKE INFORMATION | PHIVOLCS ADVISORY
newsArticles.summary:
EARTHQUAKE INFORMATION | PHIVOLCS ADVISORY

A Magnitude 2.3 earthquake was recorded by PHIVOLCS today, 26 June 2026, at 7:09 PM, with its epicenter located 18 km North 22° West of Sarangani Island, Davao Occidental, at a depth of 81 km.

At this magnitude, no damage and aftershocks are expected.

Although this was a minor earthquake, it serves as a reminder that our municipality should always be prepared for any emergency.

🔹 Safety Reminders:
✅ Stay calm and avoid spreading unverified information.
✅ Familiarize yourself with safe evacuation areas and emergency exits.
✅ Prepare and maintain your emergency go bag.
✅ During strong earthquakes, remember: DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON.
✅ Follow only official updates from PHIVOLCS and LDRRMO-Titay.

Let us remain vigilant and always practice disaster preparedness. Being prepared today can save lives tomorrow.

newsArticles.title: BRGY. MATE FIRE INCIDENT
newsArticles.summary:
BRGY. MATE FIRE INCIDENT
12 February 2026

At approximately 2:00PM, LDRRMO personnel under the supervision of George D. Carabaña Jr., responded to a fire incident at the residence of Merryjane Husain and Rolando Husain in Mate, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. Initial assessment determined that the cause of the fire was a lightning strike during the weather disturbance.

Upon receiving the report, our team immediately proceeded to the area to conduct emergency response operations, ensure the safety of the occupants, and assist in fire control and damage assessment. We continue to remind everyone to remain alert during inclement weather, as lightning strikes can pose serious risks to both lives and property.
